title: Gotrade Daily: Oracle & Adobe Report, Oil Tops $100
summary: Oracle and Adobe report tonight as oil tops US$100 and bond yields near 5%. Here is the watchlist for tonight's US session: ORCL, ADBE, XOM, NVDA, NET.
body_markdown:
At the same time, oil breaking above US$100 and the 10-year yield closing in on 5% have revived inflation worries. That mix leaves tonight's session pulled in several directions at once.


## Tonight's Watchlist


Stock Movement What to Watch


[ORCL](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/orcl/) Reports Q1 FY2027 tonight Cleanest read on cloud and AI-infrastructure demand; consensus around US$1.74 EPS and US$19.1B revenue


[ADBE](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/adbe/) Reports after the close Tests whether AI is adding users and monetization, not threatening pricing; consensus around US$6.07 EPS


[XOM](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/xom/) Lifted by the oil surge Brent up 3.4% to about US$101, a roughly seven-week high; energy as a haven


[NVDA](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) High attention, mixed signals DOJ probing its Groq licensing deal; new Australian data-center buildout


[NET](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/net/) Jumped 10.5% after hours Upbeat outlook; management says the opportunity is "larger than the business"


## Tonight's Catalysts


### Oracle and Adobe, two AI bellwethers report tonight


**Oracle ([ORCL](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/orcl/) )** and **Adobe ([ADBE](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/adbe/) )** both report after the close tonight. Oracle is the market's cleanest gauge of cloud and AI-infrastructure demand, with consensus near US$1.74 EPS and US$19.1B in revenue. Adobe tests whether AI is expanding its user base and monetization rather than threatening its pricing power. Together, the two prints could set the tone for tech trading ahead.


### Oil tops US$100 and energy inflation returns to focus


Brent crude rose 3.4% to about US$101 a barrel, its highest in roughly seven weeks, lifted by supply worries tied to geopolitical tension. **ExxonMobil ([XOM](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/xom/) )** and other energy names benefit, but the broader tape suffers because the move revives inflation fears and the odds of another rate hike.
